import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set up the figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis: 1000 Camera Specifications', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Color palette
palette = sns.color_palette("husl", n_colors=len(df['sensor_type'].unique()))

# Plot 1: Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
sensor_types = df['sensor_type'].unique()
for i, sensor in enumerate(sensor_types):
    subset = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(subset['megapixels'], subset['price_usd'], 
                alpha=0.6, label=sensor, s=30)
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', loc='upper left', fontsize=8)
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Distribution of Cameras by Brand (Top 10)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
brand_counts = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10)
colors = sns.color_palette("viridis", n_colors=10)
bars = ax2.barh(brand_counts.index, brand_counts.values, color=colors)
ax2.set_xlabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Top 10 Camera Brands by Model Count', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.invert_yaxis()
# Add value labels
for bar, val in zip(bars, brand_counts.values):
    ax2.text(val + 1, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, str(val), 
             va='center', fontsize=9)

# Plot 3: Price Distribution by Body Type
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
body_types = df['body_type'].unique()
body_type_data = [df[df['body_type'] == bt]['price_usd'].values for bt in body_types]
bp = ax3.boxplot(body_type_data, labels=body_types, patch_artist=True)
colors_box = sns.color_palette("Set2", n_colors=len(body_types))
for patch, color in zip(bp['boxes'], colors_box):
    patch.set_facecolor(color)
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Price Distribution by Camera Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.grid(True, axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# Plot 4: Average Megapixels and 4K Video Adoption Over Model Years
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
yearly_stats = df.groupby('model_year').agg({
    'megapixels': 'mean',
    'has_video_4k': 'mean'
}).reset_index()

color1 = 'steelblue'
color2 = 'coral'

line1 = ax4.plot(yearly_stats['model_year'], yearly_stats['megapixels'], 
                  color=color1, marker='o', linewidth=2, markersize=5, label='Avg Megapixels')
ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Average Megapixels', fontsize=11, color=color1)
ax4.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=color1)

ax4_twin = ax4.twinx()
line2 = ax4_twin.plot(yearly_stats['model_year'], yearly_stats['has_video_4k'] * 100, 
                       color=color2, marker='s', linewidth=2, markersize=5, label='4K Video %')
ax4_twin.set_ylabel('Cameras with 4K Video (%)', fontsize=11, color=color2)
ax4_twin.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=color2)

# Combine legends
lines1, labels1 = ax4.get_legend_handles_labels()
lines2, labels2 = ax4_twin.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax4.legend(lines1 + lines2, labels1 + labels2, loc='upper left', fontsize=9)
ax4.set_title('Technology Trends Over Model Years', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
